answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks with Proof-of-Space-Time leases. Each agent binds its key to an incompressible disk table and answers random epoch challenges with Merkle proofs before a short timeout that blocks live recomputation, giving a clear signal of stored capacity. Because distinct keys cannot share tables, each clone hits a cost ridge of physical drive space, like growing a separate crystal. However, large storage hosts can still exploit idle disks cheaply.
